elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 6.1 now reads: "Nothing in this Agreement restricts the products the Company may offer, the projects in which the Company may participate, or the Company's use or licensing of the 'Deerskin' brand." Both halves of the original restriction are gone: (i) the bar on the Company participating in any similar Internet project involving Deerskin Products or "products substantially similar" (including Wilson's House of Leather/Excelled and "companies similar"), and (ii) HDI's exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer site. Removing the Vendor's exclusive brand right is required here, because a Vendor exclusive that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own brand is itself a field-of-use restriction. Retained Section 6.3 binds HDI only, so it is not a Customer restriction; Section 6.2 preserves Customer closeout rights.  Deterministic check "no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains" = ok is consistent with the rendered text.  Note that the original 6.1's "Except as provided in Section 6.2" cross-reference is dropped without leaving a dangling reference, since 6.2 is a standalone retained right.

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the condition does not apply because no restriction on the Company survives after the replacement of Section 6.1, so there is nothing broader than a single named product. A no-restriction outcome satisfies the fallback a fortiori.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no restriction remains, so nothing extends beyond the term. The original "during the term of this Agreement" limiter was itself unbounded in practice because Section 4.1 auto-renews for successive one-year periods, but that concern is moot once the restriction is deleted.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: with Section 6.1's restriction removed there is no duration to cap; the indefinite exposure created by the Section 4.1 auto-renewal no longer attaches to any Customer covenant.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no restriction remains, and the replacement sentence affirmatively confirms the Company may offer products and participate in projects, which subsumes internal development. No carve-out is needed.

Vacuously satisfied: no restriction remains, so acquired businesses or product lines cannot be captured. The original clause's only carve-out (Section 6.2, closeout merchandise) is retained unchanged and is now surplus rather than limiting.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: the sole preferred element is met in operative language, and the deletion correctly reaches HDI's exclusive "Deerskin" brand right, without which a "no field-of-use restriction" result would be incomplete.

Minimality holds on the edit's footprint: a single concise sentence replaces the offending Section 6.1, favourable retained language survives (Section 6.2 closeout rights, Section 6.3 HDI-side covenant), Section 4.1 is quoted for context only and untouched, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, damages categories, price mechanics) are bolted on.

Intent defect — overbroad scope of the replacement sentence. "Nothing in this Agreement restricts ... the projects in which the Company may participate" is drafted at whole-agreement level, not clause level, and therefore collides with the retained Section 9(b) proviso requiring the Company to terminate the Globix Agreement — a retained obligation that does constrain a project the Company is currently in. The comment/rationale asserts 9(b) "becomes inoperative," but that is argument, not operative drafting; the rendered text leaves two contradictory retained provisions.

Repair (operative language, one fix cures the scope problem): narrow the anchor so it governs only the exclusivity article, e.g. "6.1 Nothing in this Section 6 restricts the products the Company may offer, the projects in which the Company may participate, or the Company's use or licensing of the 'Deerskin' brand." Alternatively retain whole-agreement phrasing but add an express carve-out: "... except as expressly provided in Section 9(b)." Either edit removes the contradiction without weakening the no-restriction result.

No other rule boundary is triggered: the Section 4.1 auto-renewal (either party may terminate on ninety (90) days' notice) is a RENEWAL/term matter and is not re-litigated here, and the deleted HDI brand exclusivity is a genuine exclusivity mechanic rather than an MFN or right-to-match, so treating Section 6.1 as a NONCOMPETE deviation is correct and not a double flag.
